dialect.detail: IBM mainframe COBOL migrated to UNIX/GnuCOBOL via DLXMIG (Deluxe Financial Services migration). CBL SQL directive with QUALIFIER CICS BINDFILE indicates DB2 precompiler. DLXMIG comments replace IBM-PC/IBM-370 with UNIX and change PROGRAM-ID quoting style. RSD- file assignments suggest GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL RSD convention post-migration.

purpose.domain_detail: Deluxe Financial Services weekly billing report processing - NACHA ACH tape billing, invoice counts, credit reason codes, due-Deluxe totals by ACH tape number
purpose.summary: Two-pass batch program that creates a weekly billing report for Deluxe Financial Services. Pass 1 reads a 545 billing transaction file and builds a work file; Pass 2 reads the work file along with NACHA parameters (575), invoice files (I8929I/P/E), and produces a 132-character printed report with billing summaries, medium breakdowns, credit analysis, and ACH tape totals.

notable_features: EXEC SQL with DB2 QUALIFIER CICS BINDFILE directive
DLXMIG migration comments replacing IBM mainframe targets with UNIX
Indexed file access (I550 with RECORD KEY and FILE STATUS)
Multiple COPY statements (9 copybooks: T0545I, T0575I, T0550I, T8929I, T8929O, T8929W, etc.)
Two-pass batch architecture with intermediate sort work file
127 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural design
verdict.notes: Source is truncated to first 16000 chars of a 120KB file. The DLXMIG migration markers clearly show this was originally IBM mainframe COBOL adapted for UNIX execution, likely GnuCOBOL. The CBL SQL directive and has_exec_sql=true confirm embedded DB2 SQL. No EXEC CICS despite the BINDFILE reference in the CBL directive. Program is from Deluxe Financial Services (check printing/financial services company), written 1998 with revisions through 2011.
